content:
sanjay: Heads up — last 2 hours saw p99 latency regressions on 8k-window runs. spike correlates with sustained burst at ~600rps. not constant but very noisy.
mei: Any new kernel rollouts or dispatch changes around the time window?
sanjay: No kernel build changed. We did flip an adaptive batching heuristic yesterday (`enable_microburst_shaping=true`) to try to tighten p50.
lina: I pulled a flamegraph from the live canary at 10:42. main tail is queuing + KV cache miss paths. sending snippet: 
```
flamegraph: queuing 45% -> kv-lookup 25% -> kernel-select 15%
kv cache evict rate spiked from 0.8% -> 4.3%
```
ana: ops-bot dropped a deploy around 10:35 but it was a config change for autoscale only.
mei: If KV evictions rose that high maybe prefix cache gets fragmented with continuous batching delays. Short sequences sit in queue longer => cache TTL semantics evict earlier.
sanjay: That fits. We saw p95 degrade less than p99. p50 still down. Trying to optimize for p50 via microbatch shaping may be damaging the tail.
lina: Quick repro on staging: run steady 500rps with mixed seq lengths (avg 512, 10% 8192) and compare two configs: 
A) max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=8, enable_microburst_shaping=true
B) max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=20, enable_microburst_shaping=false
Results: A p99=420ms, B p99=310ms (but p50 higher in B).
mei: So aggressive low max_wait improves p50 at cost of p99 — classic tradeoff.
sanjay: But interestingly kernel selection differs: with A we saw more frequent small-kernel (fast path) choices for small batches; with B more large-kernel invocations but amortized by batching for long seqs.
ana: Are we seeing different kernel fallbacks due to KV cache misses? Kernel runtime logs show extra cold path entries when kv-miss rate climbs.
lina: Yes. logs: `kernel_select: fallback_to_generic=true reason=kv_miss`
sanjay: Profiling notes: when a long seq (8k) waits in queue because we hold max_wait tight, it ends up not joining a large batch and metastatically triggers extra kernel switch later when it finally executes. messy.
mei: Proposed tweak: introduce per-request dynamic max_wait_ms based on request seq_len and kv_cache_score. Short seqs keep low max_wait, long seqs get higher latency budget so they can coalesce.
ana: That sounds promising. How to compute kv_cache_score?
lina: Simple heuristic: kv_cache_score = 1 - estimated_prefix_probability. Use recent prefix hits in the node to score. If low hit, give more wait to allow other requests with similar prefixes to arrive.
sanjay: Experiment plan: deploy A/B two policies on canary pool (5% traffic). Measure p50/p95/p99 and kernel-switch count, kv-evict rate, and tokens/s cost.
mei: Targets: we want p99 < 350ms for 8k runs while keeping p50 within 10% of current. Also keep additional per-token cost delta < 6%.
lina: Implementation detail: change scheduler to expose per-request wait_budget_ms. Add heuristic in dispatch where we compute wait_budget_ms = clamp(base_wait * weight(seq_len, kv_score), 2, 50).
sanjay: Also add tracing: `scheduler.wait_budget`, `kv.hit_probability`, `kernel.choice` to correlate traces.
ana: Can infra handle increased trace cardinality? ops-bot: tracing quota alert if >10% increase.
mei: We'll sample 5% of requests for full trace, rest aggregate metrics only.
lina: Quick experiment on staging showed promising numbers: dynamic-wait reduced kernel-switches by 23% and p99 by ~18% for long sequences, p50 increased ~6%.
sanjay: Great. Rollout steps: 1) canary 5% w/ sampling 5% 2) monitor for 30m p99/p95 and kernel-switch 3) if stable, bump to 25% 4) monitor 1h 5) full rollout.
ana: Add auto-fallback: if p99 spikes above threshold or kv-evict rises >2x baseline, revert to default.
mei: Also would like to run microbench that sweeps max_batch_tokens and this dynamic wait multiplier to find Pareto frontier (p99 vs throughput). I can run 48-hour grid.
sanjay: Please include a short bash harness we can use: 
```bash
for wait in 5 10 20 40; do 
  run_load --rps 500 --seq_dist mix512_8k --scheduler_wait=$wait --out metrics/$wait.json
done
```
lina: I'll add a kernel-level trace to count `kernel_switches` per minute.
ana: Anything else before we kick canary?
mei: One more: make sure the model cache TTL is not tied to queue time; if TTL is wall-clock we need to instrument queuing_time to ensure we don't evict while in-queue.
sanjay: Good catch — current TTL is based on last_access which we increment on queue arrival; need to check if we call that on enqueue vs on execute.
lina: I'll audit enqueue vs execute hooks.
ana: Kicking canary in 15. ops-bot: canary started on pool-rt-3 with config `dynamic_wait_v1` at 11:20.
ops-bot: alert: tracing-quota usage +3% (sampled traces running).
sanjay: Monitoring window now. Will post results in this thread in ~40m. :thumbsup:
